_comment: Pronunciation lexicon (narration skill, PRONUNCIATION.md). Only respell and accept change narration; say/ipa/lang/sources/decoy/note/probe are the record. Looked up with lookup_pronunciation.py and probed with probe_names.py run --write, first with robert on the GPU host and again on the build host with this video's voice, leo (2026-10-11, ftts 0.1.11, FrankenWhisper, 3 carriers, control + decoy). Entries whose probe found no winner carry a note with the decision and its reason. Re-probe when the voice or ftts version changes; the owner's pronunciation overrides every entry. The piece name A has no entry on purpose: narrate.py treats every word key as a name, and the article 'a' would then be checked as one. Not respelled: the script also uses 'A' as the article ('A card', 'A row'), and a respelling would apply to both. The letter was heard as 'A' (letters: ay) in 2 of 3 carriers; in 'like A in algebra' ASR wrote a lowercase 'a', which cannot tell ay from uh (the decoy 'uh' was heard as nothing). Narration triage checks every sentence where A is a piece name (ASR casing, then the vowel's length and glide). Top-level accept and the digit phrases (narration pass 1, leo, 2026-10-11) normalize what ASR writes for the same sound: byte/bite, British spellings, the letter X for 'ex', and byte values in the script's spoken form ('two fifty-six'), since the scorer would read 256 as 'two hundred and fifty six'.

RaptorQ.note: leo, 2026-10-11: Raptor Q, Raptor queue and Raptor-Q heard 'Raptor Q' 3/3 (decoy REEP-tor-kyoo 'Reap Torque'); the plain spelling was heard 'raptor cube' once, so it is not read, and 'raptor cube' is not accepted.

ex-or.owner: 2026-10-12, after the first cut: 'ex-or' sounded like 'exer'. Both syllables are full: EKS-OR, the second as in 'oar'. The ASR heard 'X or' for the reduced reading too, so it cannot judge this; spectrograms do. In 'B ___ C is four.' the vowel after the 'ks' lasts 440 ms with its energy under 1 kHz for 'ex-oar'; 'X-or' and 'ecks-or' gave 135 ms. 'ex or' and 'ex-or' are no longer read.
ex-or.note: leo, 2026-10-11: plain and 'ex or' PASS 3/3 (heard 'X or', 'XOR'; decoy Zor 'Zor'); caps EKS-or read as letters. The script tokenizes 'ex-or' as 'ex' + 'or'; phrases map 'x or', 'xor', 'exor' back.

acoustic.method: 0-4 kHz spectrogram crops of every occurrence in the chosen reads (37 in 31 sentences), read by eye in each of three builds; a band-energy track (80-1300 Hz against 1300-4000 Hz, 5 ms frames) beside them as a pointer. Length = from the end of the ks to where the second formant leaves the band under 1.3 kHz (the next sound). Evidence for the eye, about +-0.04 s.
acoustic.seen: With ex-oar and ex oar the second vowel is an 'oar' everywhere: its energy stays under 1.3 kHz for its whole length, the third formant falling at its end; no read has the 'er' of the first cut. Its length depends on the sentence, not on the spelling: 0.23-0.45 s in running sentences, 0.15-0.20 s in some reads of tight formulas ('B ex-or C', 'one ex-or two', 'B ex-or E'). Hyphen and space each win in some sentences. Quoted reads are often shorter (quoted 'B ex-oar C is four.' 0.17 s, plain 0.40 s).
acoustic.probe: Eight other spellings in three quoted carriers ('B _ C is four.', 'Then A _ B _ C _ P is always zero.', "What's five _ seven?"): ex-ore, ex ore, ex-orr, ecks-ore, ex-awr, ex OR, ex-OR, ex-OAR. None was reliably longer than ex-oar; ex-orr and ecks-ore added pauses, ex-awr was heard 'XR', ex-OAR was read with extra syllables. The respellings stay ex-oar and ex oar.
acoustic.fix: The chooser's rate term prefers the faster read, which is the one with the short vowel. Where a longer read existed it is named in picks.tsv (8 sentences). What stays under 0.22 s is listed in the director's report.

acoustic_michael.method: probe_names.py run (control, decoy, three carriers) for every word, then 0-8 kHz spectrograms with band levels (80-1300, 1300-4000, 4000-10000 Hz); length = the stretch after the ks where the low band dominates by 10 dB or more.
acoustic_michael.probe: In 'B _ C is four.': the plain spelling ex-or leaves 0.10 s (the 'exer' the owner heard with leo); ex-oar 0.29 s plain and 0.23 s quoted; ex oar 0.37 s plain (after a 0.12 s gap) and 0.20 s quoted. ex-ore and ex OR add a syllable ('X or a C', 'X or O, C'). The respellings stay ex-oar and ex oar. In the default carriers the ASR passes ex-or and ex-oar 3/3 and ex oar 2/3 ('ex-ahwa' once, sentence-final).
acoustic_michael.seen: michael reads faster than leo: in the first build 17 of 37 chosen occurrences were 0.12-0.19 s, all in formulas or before a stop ('ex-or card', 'ex-or packet'). Picks name the longer read where one exists; see picks.tsv and the director's report for what stays short.

_phrases_note: Director pass, leo, 2026-10-12. The last phrase undoes a repeat that fw adds at the end of line 15_3: after '...one time in 256' the line transcript goes on ', and they fill it up to the last 10 to 16 slots.', a clause of the sentence before. The sheet shows one utterance (the last sentence is 5.0 s for its 22 syllables) and every repeated word has a 1 ms time at the last sample of the file (17.242-17.251 s); the take's own transcript has no repeat. The same thing happened on 03_6 ('Is it useful? Is it useful?', the second copy at 4.700-4.702 s of a 4.75 s line) until another read of its middle sentence was chosen; no phrase was needed there. The fractions 7/8, 6/8 and 4/8 are how fw writes 05_2's 'Seven eighths, times six eighths, times four eighths.'; the edges gate looked for the word 'eighths' at the sentence's end. In the take the last word is whole: its 'ths' runs 0.15 s and decays about 20 dB before the file ends. 'is it useful? is it useful?': with the quoted read of 03_6's last sentence fw writes the question twice, the second copy with 1 ms word times at the last sample of the line (4.700-4.702 s of 4.75 s); the sheet shows one utterance of 0.9 s. michael, 2026-10-12: fw glues the piece name to the word in 'B ex-or C is four.' (BXORC, BXOR C, BX or C); the B is there, 0.27 s of 'ee' before the ks in the plain ex-oar read, so these spellings are mapped back.
